Test a weighted combination using inverse_error to see if error‑based weighting improves over the mean, given unstable ranking and many correlated groups.
test a different weighting scheme (softmax_neg_error) to see if a non‑linear weight improves over inverse_error, given unstable ranking and trend dominance.
try a robust DBA combination on the full pool given trend dominance and unstable ranking.
Test a robust trimmed mean to see if trimming the worst 20% improves over mean and DBA, given trend dominance and unstable ranking.
The series is trend_dominated with unstable ranking; a robust median may perform well.
test a weighted combination on the smaller, more stable pool4 using inverse_error weights to see if focusing on low‑error models improves over trimmed_mean.
Try a per‑horizon weighted combination on the stable pool4 to capture horizon‑specific strengths while staying robust to ranking instability.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a robust combination like weighted softmax on a stable subset (pool4) may outperform trimmed mean.

Test a weighted combination on the full pool with the default weight handle w1 to see if a simple weighted mean improves over trimmed_mean, exploring the idea that a more nuanced weighting might capture complementary errors.
use per‑horizon top‑k mean weights on a stable subset

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 11 backtested attempts, score 0.9713. Series context: trend strength 0.9824 and seasonal strength 0.3964; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.068); 4 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 1.153.
